brief: US tech rebound spread into Asia (Hynix, Samsung, KOSPI up), fading as oil rises, leaving the desk asking whether this is an oversold QQQ bounce or a sustainable recovery. Activity stays muted ahead of FOMC, BoC, ECB and BoJ decisions and earnings from 44% of S&P 500 market cap led by MSFT, GOOG, AMZN and INTC, with recent bounces read as easing selling rather than renewed buying. Neoclouds remain pressured on Musk's financing and consolidation comments. AI credit spreads narrowed from Friday's wides but stay the key watch item. Cadence beat and raised, citing AI-driven EDA tool adoption as an incremental growth driver rather than a disruption risk. Celestica also beat and raised FY27 guidance above street, reading positive for Flex, AVGO and ANET in the US. In Europe, Orange beat and raised on Spain and France outperformance. Tieto's revenue missed worse than expected but margins beat, so it cut FY26 revenue guidance while raising margin guidance. Informa cut 2026 revenue growth guidance on Saudi disruption but kept earnings guidance, arguing most of the risk was already priced. Verizon's tone toward SpaceX hardened between Q2 and Q3 calls as the EU moved to reserve satellite spectrum against Starlink and Kuiper.
